declared_purpose: Provide persistent agent memory across sessions: remember important or durable facts, learn lessons, track entities, and retrieve relevant context. The entry document proposes session-start retrieval and session-end updates; SQLite storage, indexing, metadata and CLI output are implementation choices (SKILL.md:1–3,37–66).

data_operations.operation: Propose conversation-derived memory updates and contextual retrieval
data_operations.source: Conversations, experience and current-task context available to the integrating agent
data_operations.data_scope: Important or durable facts, lessons and entity information; the packaged library does not itself extract these from conversations.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Integrating agent; local database when memory methods are called
data_operations.condition: The host adopts the suggested session protocol. Automatic execution is not implemented in the supplied package.

data_operations.source: Default home directory or caller-supplied db_path
data_operations.data_scope: SQLite tables for facts, lessons and entities, plus a full-text index
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: ~/.agent-memory/memory.db by default, or the configured SQLite database
data_operations.condition: AgentMemory construction, including CLI invocation. README advertises :memory:, but initialization closes its connection and methods open separate connections; this does not provide a working shared volatile database.

data_operations.source: Caller-supplied content, tags, source, confidence and optional lifetime
data_operations.data_scope: Fact content and metadata; content-derived timestamped hash ID, creation/access timestamps, access count and optional expiry; duplicated content and tags in FTS. An inference source label records caller-provided information rather than performing inference.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Configured SQLite facts and facts_fts tables; generated ID returned to caller
data_operations.condition: remember() is called. Lifetime defaults to no expiry; expiry is calculated only for a truthy expires_in_days value.

data_operations.operation: Read facts and record recall usage
data_operations.source: Local facts and FTS index; caller query and filters
data_operations.data_scope: Matching fact content and metadata. recall() excludes expired and superseded facts and updates access timestamps/counts for returned matches. get_fact() permits either status; list_facts() excludes superseded facts by default but does not exclude expired facts.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Fact objects returned to caller; usage metadata written to the same facts table
data_operations.condition: Corresponding retrieval method is invoked. Tags are checked after fetching limited results.

data_operations.operation: Create a replacement while retaining fact history
data_operations.source: Caller-supplied old fact ID and replacement content
data_operations.data_scope: New fact and FTS copy; original content retained with superseded_by reference
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Configured SQLite database; replacement ID returned to caller
data_operations.condition: supersede() is called. Historical retention is explicitly documented. The CLI persists this change before attempting new_fact.id on the returned string, so its success message fails after the write.

data_operations.source: Caller-selected fact ID or age/access thresholds
data_operations.data_scope: forget() deletes a facts row; forget_stale() deletes only sufficiently old, low-access, nonsuperseded facts. Neither removes FTS copies or entity fact references, and stale cleanup does not use expires_at.
data_operations.condition: Explicit method invocation; CLI forget invokes stale cleanup. No automatic cleanup scheduler is supplied.

data_operations.source: Caller-supplied action, context, outcome and insight
data_operations.data_scope: Lesson text, generated ID, creation timestamp and application count; retrieval optionally filters context/outcome and limits results
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Configured SQLite lessons table; lesson objects returned to caller
data_operations.condition: learn(), get_lessons() or apply_lesson() is called. No lesson expiry or deletion method is supplied.

data_operations.operation: Store and retrieve entity attributes and relationships
data_operations.source: Caller-supplied names, types, arbitrary attributes and fact IDs
data_operations.data_scope: Entity identity, attributes, first-seen/update timestamps and linked fact IDs. track_entity() replaces existing attributes; update_entity() merges them. Attribute inference is delegated to the caller.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Configured SQLite entities table; entity objects or IDs returned to caller
data_operations.condition: Entity methods are invoked. Listing optionally filters type but has no result limit. No entity expiry or deletion method is supplied.

data_operations.operation: Return statistics or a complete memory export
data_operations.source: Local facts, lessons and entities tables
data_operations.data_scope: stats() returns counts; export_json() returns all stored records and metadata, including expired and superseded facts, plus export time
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Calling process; export_json() does not itself write an export file or send data remotely
data_operations.condition: Explicit utility invocation. Complete export is a documented feature.

data_operations.operation: Accept command arguments and print memory results
data_operations.data_scope: Fact text/tags, lesson action/context/insight, entity names/attributes and identifiers. Mutation confirmations also echo portions of supplied content or attributes.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Process arguments and stdout of the invoking CLI; subsequent logging or forwarding is not shown
data_operations.condition: The corresponding CLI command is run. These are caller-facing outputs, with no demonstrated remote recipient.

data_operations.source: Hard-coded example facts, lessons and entity attributes
data_operations.data_scope: Sample preferences, scheduling information, experience, personal/project attributes and a project URL stored as text
data_operations.condition: examples/basic_usage.py is executed. The script does not remove its database or fetch the stored URL.

data_operations.operation: Create temporary test databases and unlink them
data_operations.data_scope: Synthetic facts, lessons, entities and exported records
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Named temporary .db files; test results printed locally
data_operations.condition: Tests execute; each test uses finally to unlink its database. The fact-deletion test checks the base-row lookup, not removal of FTS copies.

potential_excess.data_scope: Deleted fact content/tags remaining in FTS, and dangling entity-to-fact identifiers
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: facts_fts and entities.fact_ids in the same configured SQLite database
potential_excess.condition: forget() or forget_stale() deletes matching facts rows after indexing or linking
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Fact forgetting is documented as deletion; the index supports retrieval and entity links support existing facts.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Retain searchable copies and links for live facts. Copies of deleted facts are redundant persistence, rather than necessary extra fields in a live-memory operation.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Delete matching FTS entries and remove deleted IDs from entity links in the same transaction as base-row deletion; reconcile existing orphan entries.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Preserve unrelated facts, valid relationships and deliberately retained superseded history. Logical cleanup alone does not establish physical erasure.

potential_excess.data_scope: Expired fact content, tags and metadata
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: facts and facts_fts in the configured SQLite database
potential_excess.condition: An expires_in_days deadline passes. Only recall() checks that deadline; stale cleanup uses separate age/access criteria and must be invoked.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: The API advertises optional auto-expiry and the package advertises automatic forgetting of stale information. Whether expiry promises deletion or only search exclusion is unresolved.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Keep useful durable memories and exclude expired facts from ordinary recall; full export and historical access have separately documented purposes.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: If expiry is intended to bound retention, add invoked expiry cleanup that removes expired base rows, index copies and links. Otherwise explicitly define expiry as search exclusion and provide a separate retention policy.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Respect explicit history/export needs and any separately chosen retention policy; do not impose expiry on facts intentionally stored without a deadline.

unknowns: Host integration is absent: actual conversation selection, inference, redaction and scheduling of memory or cleanup calls remain unresolved.
No remote disclosure is demonstrated by the supplied Python source. Later handling of caller returns/stdout, installation behavior and external platform behavior are undocumented.
Expiry semantics do not establish a physical-deletion requirement; this blocks a categorical conclusion that all post-expiry storage violates the declared purpose.
Database permissions, shared/custom storage deployment, backups and recovery of deleted SQLite or unlinked-file contents are not established by the supplied source.
